His coworkers know him first and foremost for his love of pranks, which sometimes go beyond the bounds of common sense. But Comrade Domov is not the least bit troubled by his sense of humor. Knowing full well that he is ultimately irreplaceable, Domov often finds ways to overshadow his stunning accomplishments by flagrantly violating the chain of command.

Comrade Verestenyets is truly a unique citizen—as the manager of the Maya Plisetskaya Theater cafeteria, she not only knows all its baking-related equipment inside and out, but also remembers the names of every ballet pose ever performed on the theater's stage. She has her repertoire for the next year committed to memory and can tell you which seat and row are best for viewing a given performance. Few people know that this remarkable woman has a PhD, but absolutely everyone she works with knows about her love for the arts. For Comrade Verestenyets, ballet is her greatest, most cherished dream.

Comrade Lebedyansky is an engineer and train builder. He was involved in the design and construction of the largest Soviet locomotives and armored trains, including the Felix Dzerzhinsky, the Joseph Stalin, and the Victory. After the war, he switched to designing cutting-edge diesel and gas turbine locomotives that attained record speeds and replaced ordinary trains on Soviet railways.  The inventor is currently involved in testing magnetic levitation or Maglev railways at Facility 3826. Vortex automatic trains will soon crisscross the entire country, extending to even the most distant reaches of the Soviet Union.
